aboutH2: Homestead for Hope: Residential Recovery for Women near Gainsborough, SK
intro: Homestead for Hope is a Christian residential program for women 18 and over, set in a restored stone farmhouse on 160 acres near Gainsborough, in southeast Saskatchewan. It is the residential arm of Choose Life Ministry, a non-profit based in nearby Carnduff. Women come with substance use, trauma, depression and anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm or an unexpected pregnancy, and stay for a 13-week Freedom Program.

The house is small on purpose. Six women live there at a time with two live-in staff, and they cook, eat and do group work together. The program costs nothing beyond a $50 application fee, and food, lodging and materials are covered by the ministry's donors.

pillars.title: A Stone Farmhouse on the Prairie near Gainsborough
pillars.body: You reach the house down a long gravel lane, and the stone farmhouse comes into view across open fields. Choose Life Ministry renovated the original building from the inside out. Downstairs there is a bright living room with windows on both sides, a dining room lined with books and a kitchen where residents make meals together. The three resident bedrooms have wooden bunks and big wardrobes. Outside, the 160 acres hold mature trees, mown lawn, a small stream and a garden plot. Gainsborough is a small village in the southeast corner of Saskatchewan, a short drive from Carnduff and the Manitoba border.

pillars.title: Thirteen Weeks Built around Freedom Session
pillars.body: The heart of the program is Freedom Session, a Christian discipleship and recovery course that works through Scripture, group discussion and honest self-reflection. Around it sit one-on-one counselling with a professional counsellor, faith-based teaching and worship, and life skills such as cooking, cleaning, communication and basic math. Everyone shares the daily work of the house. The program runs on fixed intake dates, so a group starts and finishes together. Faith is not an add-on here, and the application asks women to accept that it guides the program.

pillars.title: A Small Team Led by a Nurse
pillars.body: Kassie Holbrook, a licensed practical nurse with about ten years of nursing behind her, is the Programming Director. She looks after intake, medical needs and the day-to-day running of the Homestead. Counselling comes from Kerri Keith, who holds an MA in Marriage and Family Therapy and is a CACFT associate, and Florence Fullerton, a Canadian Certified Counsellor with the same degree and a background in addictions, grief and veteran care. Two staff live in the house, and the wider Choose Life Ministry team in Carnduff supports them.

overviewH2: Homestead for Hope: Who It Is For and What It Costs
overview: The program is for women 18 and older. The centre lists substance abuse, depression and anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm behaviours, trauma and abuse, and unexpected pregnancy as the issues it helps with. Choose Life Ministry also runs pregnancy support and community outreach across Saskatchewan, so the Homestead is one part of a wider ministry.

afterOverview: Homestead for Hope does not describe a detox service, an outpatient program or a formal aftercare plan on its website, so ask about those before you apply if you need them. Women who want a secular program, or who need medical withdrawal care first, should look at other Saskatchewan options as well.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What kind of program is Homestead for Hope?
faqs.a: Homestead for Hope is a Christian, faith-based residential program for women 18 and over. Residents live in a restored stone farmhouse near Gainsborough, Saskatchewan for a 13-week Freedom Program that combines professional counselling, faith-based teaching, life skills and community living. It is the residential facility of Choose Life Ministry, a Christian non-profit.

faqs.q: How much does Homestead for Hope cost?
faqs.a: The program is free. Choose Life Ministry charges a $50 application fee once you are accepted, which secures your place. Food, lodging and program materials are all included, and the ministry is funded by donations.

The Freedom Program runs for 13 weeks and starts on set intake dates. For 2027 the centre lists intakes from January 4 to April 10, May 16 to August 14, and September 12 to December 11. Check the intake dates page on the centre's website for the current schedule.

faqs.q: Who can attend Homestead for Hope?
faqs.a: The program is for women aged 18 and older. The centre works with women facing substance use, depression and anxiety, eating disorders, self-harm, trauma and abuse, and unexpected pregnancy. The application asks about your faith background, and applicants agree that Christian faith guides the program.

faqs.q: Does Homestead for Hope offer detox?
faqs.a: The centre does not describe a detox or medical withdrawal service on its website, and recovery.com lists detox as not offered. If you are still using alcohol or drugs, ask the team how to arrange withdrawal care before your intake date.

The farmhouse sits on 160 acres near Gainsborough, in the southeast corner of Saskatchewan close to the Manitoba border. It is about 3 hours 15 minutes from Regina, about an hour from Estevan and about 2 hours from Brandon, Manitoba. The mailing address is Choose Life Ministry, PO Box 426, Carnduff, SK S0C 0S0.

Freedom Session is the Christian discipleship and recovery curriculum at the centre of the program. Homestead for Hope describes it as a way to work on the roots of life-controlling issues through Scripture, community and honest self-reflection. Residents go through it with trained leaders and the other women in the house.

faqs.q: How many women live at the Homestead at once?
faqs.a: The house has six resident beds in three bedrooms, plus two beds for live-in staff. With so few residents, groups stay small and staff know each woman well.

Kassie Holbrook, an LPN, is the Programming Director and handles programming, medical needs and intake. Counselling comes from Kerri Keith, a therapist and CACFT associate, and Florence Fullerton, a Canadian Certified Counsellor. Choose Life Ministry's wider team supports the house.

Fill in the application form on the centre's website, or call the office at 306-339-7035, Monday to Thursday from 9am to 4pm. You can also nominate someone else through the same form. Applications ask about health, substance use, mental health history and faith.
